inputs.text: [happily] Listen up: we're moving forward in time again. [excited] But dry land is still completely bare.
[curious] Totally bare? No plants at all?
[calm] Not yet, but they're coming: mosses first, then the very first green plants spread over the continents. [softly] And soon, [happily] the very first trees.
[amazed] And what's going on in the sea?
[excited] In the sea, this time is called the Devonian. [serious] The name comes from Devon, a region of England where scientists found its rocks. [happily] It's nicknamed "the age of fishes."
[playful][calm] Because there are fish of every shape! [amazed] And some have thick, fleshy fins, [gasps] almost like legs.
[happily][excited] Exactly! Tiktaalik can even lift its head out of the water, [pauses] and breathe a little air before diving back in.
[serious][softly] And one day, some of these fish dare to climb all the way out. [pauses] The very first amphibians are born: animals that live in the water AND on land, [calm] like frogs today.
[amazed] And after that, it turns into a giant forest?
[chuckles][happily] Almost! A bit later comes the Carboniferous, [serious] named that way because it formed the coal we still use today. [excited] Huge forests, and air full of oxygen...
[amazed] And giant insects flying between the trees!
[playful][calm] A dragonfly with wings wider than a dinner tray. [pauses] Life on land is only just beginning.
